title: Determinism at the Edge: Why the AI Search Is a Mock — Check

questions.prompt: Why is the AI search implemented as a deterministic mock rather than a live LLM call?
questions.explanation: Keeping AI as a deterministic mock at the edge preserves reproducibility in the domain modules, enabling exact assertions and offline development.
options: Because LLMs cannot be called from TypeScript
So the core compute path stays reproducible and exactly testable, with nondeterminism confined to the edge
To permanently avoid ever using AI in the product
Because deterministic mocks are always more accurate than real models

questions.prompt: What is the danger of placing an LLM in the middle of the gateway's fan-out path?
questions.explanation: Nondeterministic output in the core path means you can no longer assert exact values, weakening the entire test suite.
options: Downstream results become nondeterministic, so tests degrade to fuzzy checks that catch fewer bugs
It would double the number of domain modules
It would change the frontend's URL

questions.prompt: If a real LLM is added later, its output should be allowed to feed directly back into deterministic numeric calculations without validation.
questions.explanation: Model output should be treated as suggestion/presentation at the edge. If it must flow downstream, it should be snapshotted and validated at the boundary so the core stays deterministic.
